FLIGHT SCHOOL / 01

AN ORIGINAL ARCADE FLIGHT DEMO

Behind the sortie

MOONFOX 64 / The Pelagos Sortie
An original arcade flight game about a small squadron and a very large dawn.

Fly the A-07 alongside Mica, Rook, and Iva. Protect the squadron, choose an approach, and dismantle the Lantern. Everything you see and hear is generated by code.

SOURCE INFORMATION

Date: 2026-10-21 01:54 America/Vancouver.
Source inspiration: StarFox 64. All characters, spacecraft, environments, music, and mission content in MoonFox 64 are original.

Tech: my-3D2dge agent edition 0.59.1 (fixed-step clock, semantic inputs, menus, scenes, settings, saves, and synthesized audio); Three.js 0.180.0 (WebGL2 perspective renderer); JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Web Audio; esbuild 0.25.12. All runtime dependencies are embedded.

Art direction: low-poly aerospace: ivory and vermilion spacecraft, turquoise water, peach haze, and monumental industrial ruins. Original vector crew portraits.

Animation: continuous procedural flight, spring-smoothed steering, procedural maneuvers, articulated machinery, shader water, and particle effects; simulation at 120 Hz.

Testing: Four text-only Playwright/headless Chrome browser verification runs. Run 1 found one critical startup script-embedding syntax error; fixed. Run 2 passed 12 checks. Runs 3 and 4 passed all 17 boot, keyboard/gamepad mapping, horizontal/vertical inversion, pause/resume, virtual DualSense analog and arena actions, controller-disconnect, direct file opening, and full attract-playback checks. Attract reached all three acts, rescued both wingmates, exercised every ability, defeated the boss, looped, and exited on input. No screenshots, image inspection, visual review, or review subagents. Test cost: unknown. Physical gamepad verification: not performed. No screenshots, image inspection, or rendering review. Test cost: unknown.

Environment: Codex CLI; Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2 (user-provided). Browser used for checks: headless Google Chrome 154.0.8037.57 via Playwright 1.63.0.

Model: OpenAI; requested gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning effort max. Independently confirmed model identity: unknown.

Usage: Usage: Session time 37m 49s; tokens 3,607,150 total (3,535,256 input including 3,274,240 cached and 0 cache-write; 71,894 output including 16,519 reasoning); API cost $1.568396 USD (Estimated standard API token cost; not subscription billing).

ENGINE FEEDBACK

Most liked: the compact single-file distribution, exact fixed-step clock, semantic gamepad inputs, chip audio, settings persistence, and explicit API card.

Stuck or guessed wrong: the agent edition omits the full engine’s menu screens, and its orthographic views need a perspective renderer for this genre.

Most important custom system: the perspective flight renderer and a data-driven mission director with rail-to-arena transitions.

Hardest part: joining the engine’s 2D presentation to a 3D flight simulation while keeping its input, clock, sound, scenes, and saves.

Remove or overhaul: full-only APIs that remain callable as no-op stubs in the agent edition.

One change: a documented external-renderer adapter and DOM-rendered pause/settings widgets in the agent edition.

PROMPT FEEDBACK / 404299fcd4

Most liked: a concrete single-file deliverable, a clear source reference, controller-first UX, and explicit attract behavior.

Confusing: unlimited performance does not specify mission length; the source’s perspective flight requires more than the supplied engine’s default 2D views.

Hardest: making the combat, tutorials, branching encounters, squad mechanics, and boss feel like one complete mission.

One additional test: a physical DualSense playthrough covering analog steering, both inversion toggles, trigger charging, and controller reconnection.
